Article Title: As Google search result shows Sam Altman dead, company clarifies not their fault; says: This was not a manual change by Google, it is when ...
Article Text:
Google has removed incorrect information about Sam Altman

Google removes incorrect information about Sam Altman

Wikipedia page reportedly targeted by vandals

Similar false claim against Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

Google briefly displayed incorrect search results claiming that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had died, triggering confusion and jokes across social media before the company removed the information. The false result appeared on August 12 after users on Reddit and X (formerly known as Twitter) shared screenshots showing Google's search page stating that Altman had died that day. Google later confirmed the information was incorrect and said it was not the result of a manual change by the company.The incorrect search result quickly went viral after users posted screenshots on Reddit and X. Google removed the incorrect information within hours. In an X post, Google said the issue has been fixed.“Thanks for flagging - this is no longer appearing, and was not a manual change by Google,” the company said adding “When people vandalize public info sources, this can affect the information that appears in Search”.The company did not identify the specific source that caused the incorrect information to appear.According to SBS News, the incident is believed to be linked to vandalism on Sam Altman's English Wikipedia page.The report said the page's revision history showed several false edits, including claims that Altman had been assassinated and changes to his surname from "Altman" to "Gayman."Following the incident, Wikipedia reportedly restricted editing of the page, allowing only registered users to make changes in an effort to prevent further vandalism.A similar incident is now affecting Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Users on social media reported that results on Google Search are showing incorrect information suggesting Amodei had died.
Article Summary: Google briefly displayed incorrect search results claiming that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had died. The false result appeared on August 12 after users on Reddit and X (formerly known as Twitter) shared screenshots showing Google's search page. Google later confirmed the information was incorrect and said it was not the result of a manual change by the company. Google removed the incorrect information within hours.

Article Title: Jamie Dimon, whose own family is an example of American Dream, to Gen Z: You could be forgiven for giving up on American Dream, as if you look at ...
Article Text:
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon

Jamie Dimon believes that the dream remains ‘totally achievable’

JPMorgan’s American Dream initiative

Capitalism under scrutiny

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon recently said that he understands why Gen Z feels the American Dream is slipping away. Between soaring away. Between soaring house prices, rising living costs, and the looming threat of AI reshaping the labour market, young Americans could be forgiven for doubting the historic ideal. A June AP-NORC poll found only one-fifth of adults aged 18 to 29 believe the American Dream is attainable. According to a report by Fortune, in an interview with Firing Line, Dimon pointed to his own family as proof of the Dream’s resilience. His grandparents immigrated from Greece without high school diplomas but instilled a strong sense of purpose in their children and grandchildren. That legacy helped Dimon rise to lead the largest bank in the U.S., a trajectory he says reflects the Dream’s enduring possibility.Speaking to PBS, Dimon argued the Dream remains “totally achievable” for most Americans, noting that the middle class has grown and wealth has increased overall. But he warned that the bottom 20% have seen stagnant incomes for decades, leaving them in struggling neighborhoods and underfunded schools. “For them, it’s slipping,” he said, adding that this inequality is fueling polarization and anger across society.Dimon highlighted JPMorgan’s American Dream Initiative, which focuses on six areas including small business support and skills-based training, as part of efforts to expand opportunity. He urged policymakers from both parties to acknowledge inequality and work on solutions, saying: “Whether you’re a Democrat or Republican, acknowledge the problem and then start to say, ‘How can you fix it?’”Dimon, who describes himself as a “patriotic, unwoke, capitalist CEO,” admitted capitalism has flaws but insisted it remains the best system available. He cautioned against conflating systemic imperfections with alternatives, noting that every system has “bad people.” His comments echo broader debates, with figures like Larry Fink of BlackRock warning that capitalism is fueling economic anxiety by failing too many people.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said he understands why Gen Z feels the American Dream is slipping away. A June AP-NORC poll found only one-fifth of adults aged 18 to 29 believe the Dream is attainable. Dimon highlighted JPMorgan’s American Dream Initiative, which focuses on six areas including small business support.

Article Title: OpenAI finally brings ChatGPT desktop app to Linux: Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora users get ChatGPT, Work and Codex in one place
Article Text:
File image: ChatGPT

Which Linux distros are supported, and what the app actually does

Linux users have spent years watching every major AI app land on Windows and macOS first, then waiting their turn. That wait just ended. OpenAI has released a dedicated ChatGPT desktop app for Linux, rolling it out worldwide on Tuesday in preview, bundling ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work and Codex into a single native experience.The company pitched it as closing the last gap in its desktop lineup. Linux was one of the most-requested platforms for the desktop app, OpenAI said, and the launch extends ChatGPT and Codex across every major desktop operating system. On paper it's a routine port. For a developer community that has been asking loudly, and for a long time, it reads differently.Support at launch covers Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and 26.04 LTS, Debian 13, and Fedora 43 and 44, across both x64 and ARM64, shipping as .deb and .rpm packages. That list looks thin next to the hundreds of distributions out there, but these are the bases for a long tail of downstream flavours, which should run the app fine as a result.What you get isn't just a chat window in a new wrapper. OpenAI positions the desktop app as a workspace: parallel projects, documents and spreadsheets opened and inspected in place, browser and computer-use workflows, scheduled tasks set up inside an existing chat, and Codex running alongside ChatGPT rather than in a separate tool.OpenAI isn't first here, though. Anthropic shipped a Claude desktop app for Linux roughly a month ago, and cast a wider net with it, supporting Ubuntu 22.04 or later and Debian 12 or later.The preview tag on OpenAI's build suggests the polish is still coming.
Article Summary: OpenAI releases ChatGPT desktop app for Linux on Tuesday. The company says Linux was one of the most-requested platforms for the app. Support covers Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and 26.04, as well as Debian 13 and Fedora 43 and 44.

Article Title: In 2015, Steve Ballmer and his wife Connie founded Ballmer Group that has donated over $8 billion since, 11 years later they are changing where ...
Article Text:
Steve Ballmer and wife Connie (Image Source: Youtube/ 60 Minutes)

Ballmer Group to create three independent regional offices

MoveUp Southeast Michigan

MoveUp LA

MoveUp Washington

Why Steve and Connie Ballmer are making the change

Ballmers have donated billions over the years

Former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer and his wife Connie are reportedly changing the way their philanthropy donations are made. The couple founded Ballmer Group in 2015 and have donated more than 8 billion over the past two decades. According to a report by Fortune, they are now planning to spin off the Ballmer Group's three regional offices into independent nonprofits while continuing to fund them. The move is aimed at bringing funding decisions closer to local communities and leaders. Steve and Connie Ballmer said the new structure will help ensure the organisations remain long-term resources while the Ballmer Group focuses on national initiatives that improve economic mobility.As stated in the report, Steve and wife Connie Ballmer will make the group’s regional office in three separate nonprofits:The organisations will operate independently, build their own boards and continue their existing work while adapting to local needs. Staff in each region will transition to the new organisations over the next year, while current funding commitments to grantees will continue without disruption.Each of the three regions has a personal connection to the Ballmers. Steve Ballmer grew up in Southeast Michigan, the couple owns the Los Angeles Clippers in California, and Washington is their home state."Our intention is to ensure that these local philanthropies can be permanent, ongoing resources in each region, while we concentrate our national efforts on advancing economic mobility in new ways," Steve and Connie Ballmer said in a joint statement.Ballmer Group CEO Terri Ludwig said the goal is to keep decision-making close to the communities being served. "How do we keep staying close to the work, and how do we empower our leaders?" Ludwig told Fast Company.As mentioned above, Steve and Connie Ballmer founded the Ballmer Group in 2015 after years of charitable work led by Connie Ballmer. Some of the group's biggest donations include $425 million to the University of Oregon to establish the Ballmer Institute for Children's Behavioral Health, $237.5 million to Blue Meridian Partners' Place Matters Initiative, and a pledge of up to $165 million to Communities In Schools.Connie Ballmer also made headlines earlier this year after personally donating $80 million to NPR, one of the largest gifts in the history of public media.
Article Summary: Former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer and his wife Connie are reportedly changing the way their philanthropy donations are made. The couple founded Ballmer Group in 2015 and have donated more than 8 billion over the past two decades. According to a report by Fortune, they are now planning to spin off the group's three regional offices into independent nonprofits. The move is aimed at bringing funding decisions closer to local communities and leaders.

Article Title: Oracle layoffs: Company's '6 am layoff emails' may return in next few days, as Oracle plans…
Article Text:
Oracle layoffs 2026: Company plans fresh job cuts this month after shedding 21,000 roles in a year, as AI data centre spending mounts.

Oracle has already cut 21,000 job in a single fiscal year

Every job cut is buying Oracle a bit more room to keep building data centres

Oracle’s revenue is climbing, which is what makes these layoffs land badly

The March layoffs left 600 Oracle workers fighting over severance, RSUs and H-1B support

Oracle employees have been told, in effect, to keep an eye on their inboxes. The company has drawn up plans for a fresh round of job cuts this month, Business Insider reported, citing people familiar with the plans and an internal document. The cuts could reach double-digit percentages on some teams, and managers have already been asked to submit lists of affected employees.The deadline is what makes this urgent. Oracle wants payroll reduced by the time its second quarter begins on September 1, which is barely three weeks away. And anyone who was around on March 31 knows exactly what that can look like: emails from "Oracle Leadership" arriving at roughly 6 am local time, no HR call, no manager warning, and one line doing all the work—"we have made the decision to eliminate your role." System access was cut the same morning. Employees in the US, India, Canada and Mexico were affected. Oracle declined to comment on the new plans.This would not be a fresh start so much as a continuation. Oracle's headcount fell by 21,000, or about 13%, in the fiscal year that ended May 31, taking the company from 162,000 employees to roughly 141,000. Restructuring costs jumped to $1.8 billion from $374 million a year earlier.In its annual filing, Oracle was unusually direct about why, saying the adoption of AI across its operations has already resulted in workforce reductions and may continue to.The arithmetic behind the cuts is not subtle. Oracle spent $55.7 billion on infrastructure last fiscal year and burned $23.7 billion more cash than it took in. It raised $43 billion in debt and another $5 billion through stock sales, and expects to raise about $40 billion more this year. TD Cowen had estimated in January that trimming 20,000 to 30,000 roles could free up $8-10 billion in incremental free cash flow. That number now reads less like a forecast and more like a plan.Oracle is not a company in trouble on paper. Revenue rose 17% last fiscal year and its cloud infrastructure business grew 77%. Net income jumped 95% to $6.13 billion in a recent quarter, and CEO Clay Magouyrk has pointed to $553 billion in remaining performance obligations as proof that demand for AI compute is outrunning supply. The stock disagrees. Oracle shares are down about 26% this year, hit both by anxiety over its debt load and by a wider selloff in software, on fears AI will eat traditional enterprise tools. Chairman Larry Ellison has dismissed that second worry, telling analysts in March the "SaaSpocalypse" would be someone else's problem.The March cuts left a residue Oracle hasn't cleared. More than 600 former employees signed a letter on April 17 seeking higher severance, extended healthcare, H-1B support and stock acceleration. Oracle replied that it would handle concerns individually, not as a group. A survey of 272 laid-off workers found 62% were over 40 and 27% had restricted stock due to vest within 90 days—stock that vanished on the way out. In India, severance in the earlier round broadly followed the N+2 formula, with unvested RSUs forfeited.Whether the next batch of emails arrives at 6 am is, at this point, the only detail still unknown.
Article Summary: Oracle has drawn up plans for a fresh round of job cuts this month. The cuts could reach double-digit percentages on some teams. The deadline is what makes this urgent. Oracle wants payroll reduced by the time its second quarter begins on September 1, which is barely three weeks away.

Article Title: Everything announced at 'Made by Google 2026': Pixel 11 phones, Pixel Watch 5, and a lot more AI
Article Text:
Made by Google Event 2026

The Pixel 11 and the Pro are further apart than they've ever been

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold finally shuts flat

HiLight is the reason Google wants your phone face down

Tensor G6 is behind almost every number Google quoted

Magic Capture takes the photo you'd have missed

Gemini Intelligence wants to act before you ask

Pixel Watch 5 looks the same and isn't

But the best Pixel Watch 5 features aren't here yet

Pixel Buds Pro 2 just get a new colour

Four phones, a watch, two new chips and a health platform. A big day by any measure, and almost none of it something you can hold.The Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL and Pixel 11 Pro Fold keep the camera bar and most of what surrounds it. New hardware comes down to three things: a Tensor G6, a rebuilt telephoto on the Pro, and a camera housing on the Fold reshaped so the phone finally shuts flat.The rest of the year went into software. Gemini Intelligence answering before you ask, Magic Capture taking the photo you'd have fumbled, and a Pixel Watch 5 that reads blood pressure trends without a cuff, then sits on the result for a month before saying anything. The Pixel Buds Pro 2, for their part, get a new colour and nothing else.There's one exception, and it's on the back of the Pixel 11 Pro. Google has put a ring of LEDs around the camera flash and called it HiLight. Every Nexus had one. The Pixel 2 had the last, and then always-on displays arrived and Google stopped bothering. Nine years on, the notification light is back, pointed at the wrong side of the phone on purpose.Here's everything Google announced, and the show itself runs later tonight, with Trevor Noah hosting and Stephen Curry, Alex Cooper and Peggy Gou along for the evening.The Pixel 11 and the Pro are further apart than they've ever beenThe two Pixels have less in common this year than they have in a while, though you wouldn't know it from the outside.The familiar camera bar keeps its shape, with the glass now running edge to edge into the frame rather than sitting on top, slimmest of all on the Pixel 11. The Pixel 11 got the cheerful colours and the Pro got the serious ones. Frost, Hibiscus, Pistachio and Obsidian on one side. Canyon, Olive, Fog and Matte Obsidian on the other, and that matte black is the first Google has offered on a Pro model.The Pixel 11 gets a 3,000-nit Actua panel behind Gorilla Glass Victus 2. The Pro pair gets Super Actua at 3,600 nits, which Google puts at 9 per cent brighter than last year and more than twice as scratch resistant, and is calling the toughest display it has shipped. Under the Pro models sits a vapour chamber to keep the chip from throttling during long camera sessions. All three are IP68.The cameras split the same way. A 48MP main on the Pixel 11, a 50MP main and a rebuilt telephoto on the Pro pair, and a gap in reach between the two that has never been wider. More on that below.Memory is the more consequential split, and it comes with a catch. The Pixel 11 starts at 256GB with 12GB of RAM, the highest floor a base Pixel has had. That isn't generosity. Gemini Intelligence won't run on less, so the floor had to move. The Pro pair climbs to 16GB and 512GB.Charging won't sell anybody a phone. It's still the upgrade you'll notice most often. All three clear 30 hours on Adaptive Battery, and half an hour on a cable takes the Pro XL to 75 per cent and the other two to 55. A new Extreme Charging Mode redirects the phone's whole performance budget into the battery for when you're in a rush.Pixelsnap magnets are built into the phones now instead of the case, worth up to 29 per cent faster wireless charging on the Pixel 11 Pro, 25 on the Pixel 11 and 17 on the Pro XL. A Clear Case, a silicone case and a Ring Stand go with them.The Pixel 11 is Rs 89,999, the Pixel 11 Pro is Rs 1,19,999 and the Pro XL is Rs 1,34,999. Buy either Pro and six months of Google AI Pro comes with it, which Google values at Rs 11,700.The camera housing on the Fold is now a dual pill instead of a block, and Google was oddly upfront about why. It was the thing stopping the phone from closing flush.That fix sits alongside a millimetre off the thickness, roughly a tenth off the weight, a new hinge, a soft-touch composite back, an IP68 rating, and a body Google's own testing puts at three times stronger than last year's.Both screens gain 20 per cent in brightness, and the outer one moves to Super Actua for the first time, which should matter more than the spec suggests given how much foldable time goes to the cover screen. Inside is an 8-inch Super Actua Flex panel.The camera is a 48MP main drawing 56 per cent more light than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold's, with a telephoto and 30x Super Zoom. Three features make use of the hinge itself. Made You Look plays animations on the outer screen while you frame, aimed at anyone who has tried to photograph a four-year-old. Dual Screen Preview lets your subject watch themselves pose. Rear Camera Selfie has you unfold the phone, frame yourself on the cover display and shoot with the main sensor rather than a front camera.Multitasking gets Split Screen, floating app Bubbles capped at five, drag and drop between apps, and a tabletop mode. There's 16GB of RAM, over 24 hours of battery and 50 per cent charge in half an hour. It costs Rs 1,86,999 with 512GB.The light sits in the camera bar where the flash normally goes, and it does nothing at all while the phone is face up.Two uses are there for now. The first is calls from specific contacts, each assigned its own colour, and because it works across both Phone by Google and WhatsApp, that colour holds whichever app the call arrives through. Set the phone down and Flip to Shhh silences it, while HiLight keeps a channel open for the handful of people you've picked out.The second is Gemini. The lights pulse through listening, thinking and answering, so a hands-free question doesn't end with you turning the phone over to see whether anything happened. Minor on paper, but it removes the main reason people feel self-conscious talking to an assistant in public.What Google hasn't said is whether HiLight handles ordinary app notifications, which is what the old Nexus light did best and what Nothing has built an entire design language around. It's the obvious third use, and probably the one that decides whether this is a feature or a flourish.HiLight is exclusive to the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL.Up to 20 per cent more power efficient than the G5. Browsing 25 per cent faster, apps loading 15 per cent quicker. Perfectly respectable figures, and not the ones anybody will remember this chip for.That job goes to the TPU, which gains 50 per cent more compute and funds Instant Night Sight, Magic Capture and the on-device Gemini work that used to need a round trip to a server. Google says the silicon was co-designed alongside DeepMind's model teams, which is how Gemini Nano ends up running faster and better than it did on the Pixel 10. The image signal processor was rebuilt too, and that's the less glamorous half of why the camera got quicker.Next to it sits a new security chip. Titan M3 brings post-quantum cryptography to the Pixel, guarding against decryption capabilities that don't exist yet and are widely expected to, and it carries the same Common Criteria certification used for SIM cards and bank cards.The everyday protections are easier to picture. Call Screen still answers unknown numbers and reports who's calling and why, and Scam Detection listens for the conversational patterns scammers use and warns you mid-call.Magic Capture is Google's replacement for burst mode, and it works from a fairly honest premise, which is that most people are worse at timing a shutter than they think.One swipe in the camera app opens it. From there it records video and pulls high-quality stills out of that video at the same time, cropping and unblurring them without being asked. You tap once and the timing stops being your problem. If any single feature from this event ends up in daily use, it's likely this one.Underneath it, the hardware moved too, and Google spent most of that budget on zoom. The Pro telephoto has been rebuilt around a sensor taking in 32 per cent more light and now reaches 120x, the longest Google has offered. More useful in practice is the new 50MP main on a 1/1.3-inch sensor with 2x optical quality, covering the 1x to 3x range where most photographs get taken. The Pixel 11 and the Fold share a 48MP main with 30x Super Zoom.Camera Looks lets you build and save your own film styles for HDR+ shots. Google has tied it firmly to Real Tone, insisting a heavily stylised look still has to render skin tones properly, which is a promise worth testing.Instant Night Sight cuts low-light capture time by up to 4.5 times on the Pro. The complaint about Night Sight was never the photograph it produced. It was how long you had to hold still for it.Video gets Pro Stable Video up to 8K through Video Boost, plus a new Creator tab with trimming and reordering tools, a Teleprompter, improved Speech Enhancement and clips that save themselves into project albums.A friend texts asking whether you're free, and your calendar surfaces on its own. Someone sends a restaurant, and the phone has it open and ready to book.That's the promise. Whether it lands as useful or exhausting comes down to how often it guesses right, and Google is keen to point out that you decide what data feeds it and can change that at any point.Two quieter changes look more dependable. Voice-to-text now strips filler words on its own, so the ums go and what you said arrives formatted. Writing help reads what's on screen and shapes replies towards how you write rather than towards a generic corporate register.Live Translate has been extended to video, podcasts and voice notes as they play, and Circle to Search has moved into the Pixel Camera, so you can identify an object, zoom into something far away or translate a sign without leaving the viewfinder.This is also the reason the Pixel 11's memory floor moved.Google kept the design, which was the easiest call it had to make all morning. The domed Actua 360 display and the pebble case both return, now in Obsidian, Fog, Olive and Canyon, with Olive on an all-new Satin Pyrite casing and Canyon exclusive to the 41mm.The rest of it changed. Qualcomm's Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 Accelerated runs Wear OS 7 at what Google calls 20 per cent faster than the Pixel Watch 4, with 64GB of storage. The screen peaks at 3,000 nits, and satellite SOS, ultra-wideband, dual-frequency GPS and 5 ATM water resistance are all included.The 45mm is rated for 40 hours with the always-on display and the 41mm for 30, though whether anyone wears this to bed comes down to charging: 15 minutes on the dock buys 15 hours.Watch faces get motion for the first time through a design called Weave, alongside a Chronograph option and the ability to generate a face from a written prompt. A Stephen Curry special edition stays in the US. Pricing starts at Rs 42,900.Everything new about this watch arrives in September, which is an unusual thing for a launch to concede.Health Guardian is the new umbrella over the watch's alerts and trend reports, and two of those reports are doing the heavy lifting. Blood Pressure Trends reads the shape of your pulse wave and how fast it travels beneath your skin, then works out whether your pressure has been running high across a full calendar month. Insulin Resistance Trends does something comparable for metabolic health, weaving heart rhythm, sleep quality and daily movement into an estimate of how hard your body is working to clear glucose. No blood, no cuff, no fasting, no appointment.Each reports once, on the first of the month, and that restraint is the entire design. Blood pressure moves around all day, and a daily number would hand you anxiety and nothing to do with it.The science isn't thin. Google trained the blood pressure model on billions of minutes of data from more than half a million people and tested it against 24-hour ambulatory monitoring, the clinical gold standard, with the research peer-reviewed in Nature.The caveats are stated just as plainly. Neither feature diagnoses anything, neither screens for hypertension or diabetes, neither should inform a decision about medication, and neither is meant for anyone pregnant. Both land on the Pixel Watch 3, 4 and 5 and on Fitbit Air, alongside Sleep Breathing Quality, which tracks how blood oxygen shifts overnight. Loss of pulse detection carries over, and breathing emergency detection stays limited to certain EU markets.The fitness work is on the same September clock. A Readiness Score tells you before a session whether to push or recover, strength and HIIT circuits can be built in the Google Health app and pushed to the wrist with audio and visual cues through every set and rest, over 50 exercise types are tracked, and a new Key Metrics view handles the review afterwards.Sleep gets Bedtime Automations, Smart Wake alarms and a rebuilt Morning Brief. Sitting above all of it is Google Health Coach, built with Gemini and locked behind Google Health Premium, which writes training plans that adapt to you and folds in Cycle Health. Three months come free with the watch, and it's bundled into Google AI Pro and AI Ultra.No new earbuds this year. The Pixel Buds Pro 2 pick up an Olive finish matching the Pixel 11 Pro and the Satin Pyrite casing on the Pixel Watch 5, and that's the whole update.Everything else carries over from 2024. The Tensor A1 chip, Silent Seal 2.0 noise cancellation, 11mm drivers, an IP54 rating, and roughly eight hours of listening with ANC switched on, or about 30 with the case.
Article Summary: The Pixel 11 and the Pro are further apart than they've ever been. The Pixel Buds Pro 2, for their part, get a new colour and nothing else. A new Extreme Charging Mode redirects the phone's whole performance budget into the battery for when you're in a rush.

Article Title: Months after Michael Dell and his wife Susan Dell's $6.25 billion donation, Department of Treasury announces new 'paycheck rules' for Trump Accounts
Article Text:
Representative Image

US Treasury proposes new Trump Accounts paycheck rules

“Trump Accounts are giving American families a new way to build wealth from day one,”

“Today, Treasury is publishing guidance that will help families grow Trump Accounts by allowing employers to contribute up to $2,500 tax-free each year for employees’ dependents and giving employees the option to contribute pre-tax dollars directly to those accounts,”

Who can contribute to Trump Accounts

Employer participation in Trump Accounts

“We saw early adoptions, and I think many more are considering it, and this guidance is going to help,”

The US Treasury Department and Internal Revenue Service (IRS) have proposed new rules for Trump Accounts. These new rules will allow employers and employees to contribute to Trump Accounts through workplace payroll systems. The latest rules come months after Dell Technologies founder and CEO Michael Dell and his wife Susan Dell pledged $6.25 billion to help fund the child savings initiative. Sharing the new rules, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the guidance will allow employers to contribute up to $2,500 tax-free each year for employees' dependent children and will allow workers to make pre-tax paycheck contributions directly into the accounts.In December 2025, Michael Dell revealed that the Michael and Susan Dell Foundation plans to commit $6.25 billion to the savings program, formerly known as Trump Accounts and later renamed Invest America accounts. The donation is intended to provide $250 to the accounts of 25 million American children when the program begins, exceeding the foundation's total charitable giving over its previous 26 years.The Treasury Department and IRS released the proposed regulations this week outlining how employers can establish and fund Trump Accounts, also known as 530A accounts.Under the proposal, qualifying employer contributions would be excluded from an employee's gross income, and employers could also allow workers to fund their dependent children's accounts through pre-tax payroll deductions.Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement.Bessent added.The proposal is now open for public comment, with a hearing scheduled for October before the regulations can be finalised.Trump Accounts are available to any US child under 18 with a Social Security number. Children born between 2025 and 2028 are eligible for a one-time $1,000 Treasury deposit under a pilot programme designed to encourage long-term savings. According to Bessent, about 7 million children have already been enrolled.Once an account is opened, parents, guardians, grandparents and other contributors can deposit up to $5,000 annually until the year before the child turns 18. Within that limit, employers may contribute up to $2,500 per employee each year.The US Treasury said more than 50 companies have already committed to contributing to Trump Accounts for their employees, with some employers also planning to match the government's $1,000 seed contribution.Melissa Elbert, partner of wealth solutions at retirement benefits consultant Aon, said the latest guidance provides employers with greater clarity on the administrative and compliance framework for implementing the programme.Elbert said.Earlier this year, a Mercer survey of nearly 350 US employers found that only about 4% expected to introduce Trump Account contribution programmes in 2026 or 2027, while about two-thirds had already decided against participating. Others remained undecided before the Treasury released its proposed rules.
Article Summary: US Treasury proposes new Trump Accounts paycheck rules. New rules will allow employers to contribute up to $2,500 tax-free each year for employees’ dependents and give employees the option to contribute pre-tax dollars directly to those accounts. The proposal is now open for public comment.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Tim Cook: “The sidelines are not where you want to live your life. The world needs you in the arena”
Article Text:
Apple CEO Tim Cook

Quote of the day by Tim Cook

“The sidelines are not where you want to live your life.

The world needs you in the arena.”

Tim Cook’s message to young people

Cook’s call to challenge the status quo

The leadership lesson behind Cook’s words

Why the quote remains relevant

Tim Cook has often spoken about the importance of taking action, accepting responsibility and using one’s abilities to make a meaningful difference. One of his most memorable messages came during his 2015 commencement address at George Washington University, where he urged graduates not to remain passive observers when the world faces problems that need solving. Cook told students that critics and cynics would always exist, but argued that simply watching from the sidelines was not enough. Instead, he encouraged them to step forward, take risks and contribute to progress. His message continues to resonate with students, professionals and entrepreneurs who may find themselves hesitating before taking the next important step in their lives.Tim Cook delivered these words during his commencement address to George Washington University’s Class of 2015 on May 17, 2015. Speaking on the National Mall, Cook encouraged graduates to think beyond their individual careers and consider how they could contribute to solving some of the world’s biggest problems. He pointed to issues including injustice, persecution and diseases that still needed cures, telling the graduates that the world needed their energy, passion and impatience with progress.Cook’s message was essentially a call to action. The “sidelines” represent a passive position where people watch events unfold, criticise decisions or wait for someone else to take responsibility. The “arena”, by contrast, represents active participation. Cook wanted graduates to understand that meaningful change requires people who are willing to step forward, face difficult problems and accept the possibility of failure. His argument was that simply identifying problems is not enough. People also need to be willing to become part of the effort to solve them.The message was particularly significant because Cook acknowledged that people who take action will inevitably face criticism. He told graduates that there would always be “cynics and critics on the sidelines” trying to tear people down. However, he also warned about another kind of passivity: people with good intentions who make no contribution at all. By drawing this distinction, Cook suggested that good intentions alone are insufficient. What matters is the willingness to turn those beliefs into action.Cook’s speech was not simply about finding a successful career. He encouraged graduates to think about the kind of impact they wanted to have on the world. He urged them to identify their values and use those values as a guide when making professional and personal decisions. George Washington University described his message as an encouragement to combine moral beliefs with vocational aspirations and to have the courage to challenge existing ideas.Cook also connected his message to his own experiences. During the speech, he recalled his first visit to Washington in 1977 as a teenager from Alabama. He discussed his discomfort with then-Governor George Wallace, whose segregationist politics conflicted with Cook’s own values. The story helped establish one of the central ideas of his speech: people should not simply accept the circumstances around them when those circumstances conflict with what they believe is right.The quote also carries a lesson about risk. People can remain on the sidelines because taking action brings the possibility of criticism, mistakes or failure. It can feel safer to observe what others are doing, point out their mistakes and wait until the outcome is clear before getting involved. Cook’s message challenges that approach. He argued that progress requires people who are willing to accept uncertainty and participate even when success is not guaranteed.His words are particularly relevant to people at the beginning of their careers. A student may hesitate to apply for an ambitious role, an employee may avoid proposing an unconventional idea, and an entrepreneur may postpone starting a business because of the possibility of failure. Cook’s message suggests that waiting indefinitely for perfect certainty can itself become a barrier. Entering the “arena” means accepting that mistakes are possible while still deciding that participation is worthwhile.Another important element of the speech was Cook’s emphasis on challenging established ideas. He argued that great progress is possible regardless of the field a person chooses. For him, innovation was not limited to technology or business. It could also involve confronting injustice, improving society or finding solutions to problems that had remained unresolved for years.This idea reflects a broader theme in Cook’s leadership philosophy. He has frequently spoken about values and the responsibility of individuals and organisations to use their influence constructively. At George Washington University, he told graduates that their values could serve as a “North Star” and warned that a career without a sense of purpose could become little more than a job.Cook’s message extends beyond students and applies to leadership, careers and everyday decisions. Taking responsibility means moving from discussing what should change to asking what contribution you can make yourself. A person does not need to hold a powerful position to make a difference. They can begin by challenging an unfair practice, supporting an important cause, developing a useful idea or simply refusing to remain silent when action is needed.The quote also highlights the difference between criticism and contribution. It is easy to identify what is wrong with someone else’s work or with a difficult situation. It is much harder to step forward and attempt to improve it. Cook’s “arena” metaphor therefore places responsibility on the individual. If a problem matters enough to criticise, it may also matter enough to become involved in solving.More than a decade after Cook delivered the speech, the message remains relevant because the challenge he described is not limited to one generation. Every generation faces problems that require people willing to participate rather than simply observe. Technology, business, education, climate change, inequality and public health all require ideas as well as action.Cook ended his address with an even stronger message to the graduates: “History rarely yields to one person, but think and never forget what happens when it does.” He then told them, “That can be you. That should be you. That must be you.”At its core, his quote is a reminder that meaningful progress rarely comes from people who spend their lives watching from a distance. It comes from those willing to enter the arena, accept uncertainty and use their energy to make something better. For anyone standing at a crossroads, Cook’s message offers a simple challenge: do not just watch the world change. Find a way to become part of that change.
Article Summary: Tim Cook delivered these words during his commencement address to George Washington University’s Class of 2015 on May 17, 2015. His message continues to resonate with students, professionals and entrepreneurs who may find themselves hesitating before taking the next important step in their lives.

Article Title: Scientist are not happy with Spacex, Amazon and other companies’ plan to build millions of 'data centers’ in Space; raise 'Night Sky' warning
Article Text:
The SpaceX logo is displayed on a building, May 26, 2020, at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla. (Photo: AP )

What makes scientists unhappy with Space datacenters

As tech giants and aerospace startups race to launch space-based data centers, scientists are warning that hundreds of thousands of new satellites could transform Earth into a ringed planet, drastically escalating light pollution and disrupting the night sky. In a new paper titled "Rings in the Sky," University of Regina astronomy professor Samantha Lawler, alongside Aaron Boley of the University of British Columbia and Hanno Rein of the University of Toronto, warned about the severe visual and environmental impact of proposed orbital data center mega-constellations."What would the sky look like if companies actually launched the tens of thousands up to one million "AI data center" satellites that they have asked for? Well, the short answer is, horrifying. The long answer is... this paper!" Lawler wrote in a social media post highlighting the research. He wrote in another post, "Here's the future that the techbros want. Earth as a ringed planet."The warning comes as companies—including SpaceX, Blue Origin, and startups such as Starcloud and Cowboy Space propose plans that could collectively send up to 1.2 million satellites into orbit. The projected figure dwarfs the roughly 16,000 active satellites currently orbiting Earth by more than 75 times, raising severe concerns regarding space debris, orbital congestion, collision risks, and optical interference for ground-based astronomy.SpaceX has touted its proposed "Starmind" data center constellation as an eco-friendly alternative to ground facilities, arguing that harvesting continuous solar energy in orbit reduces carbon footprints and relieves pressure on terrestrial power grids. Other industry players are similarly targeting space-based solar power to fuel high-performance GPUs equipped with specialized liquid-cooling systems.However, scientists point out that to continuously harvest solar energy, these orbiting data centers must occupy specific "sun-synchronous" orbits along the polar terminator—the moving line that divides day and night on Earth.By aligning along this line, entire constellations can perpetually face the sun while circling the globe over the poles. According to the researchers, this specific trajectory will inevitably create dense, artificial ring structures around the planet.“These systems would produce large ring structures with each ring passing through the sky twice a day. The largest impacts are expected to occur during winter, where ring structures could be seen sweeping through otherwise dark skies,” the authors wrote in their paper. Because the data centers require massive solar arrays and heavy hardware, their physical size will make them exceptionally reflective.Simulations and visual models created by Lawler demonstrate that constellations from SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Cowboy Space would be prominently visible from the ground, particularly during twilight hours at 6 p.m. and again around 3 a.m. Blue Origin’s proposed "Sunrise" constellation, which spans two rings, would remain almost constantly visible during night hours in northern polar regions.The findings echo growing concerns across the scientific community regarding the rapid commercialization of Low Earth Orbit. Speaking to Space.com last month, Hugh Lewis, a professor of astronautics and space debris expert at the University of Birmingham, offered a stark assessment of the proposed constellations: “The impact on the night sky would be absolutely catastrophic."
Article Summary: Scientists warn that hundreds of thousands of new satellites could transform Earth into a ringed planet. Tech giants and aerospace startups race to launch space-based data centers. Researchers warn of severe visual and environmental impact of proposed orbital data center mega-constellations.

Article Title: Google's ex-chief scientist Jeff Dean shares last few hours at Google: Tears, lots of emotional chat, explosion of sad emojis and one minute of…
Article Text:
Jeff Dean, Google's 30th employee and chief scientist, is leaving after 27 years to lead AI startup Discovery Loop.

Jeff Dean's Google farewell party was booked for 300 and 1,500 people showed up

Why Jeff Dean stayed up till 2:30 AM answering Google chat messages

Unemployed for exactly one minute, then Jeff Dean became the co-founder of Discovery Loop

Jeff Dean spent his final night as a Google employee doing what most departing executives hand off to an auto-reply. He sat up until 2:30 in the morning answering 400 goodbye messages one by one, because his corporate account was about to expire and take every one of them with it.Speaking at the KDD Conference in Jeju, South Korea, Google's former chief scientist put up a slide with an hour-by-hour timeline of his last two days at the company he joined in 1999 as employee number 30. He later posted it on X with an apology attached: anyone who messaged him after Thursday afternoon never got a reply, because by then the laptop was shut for good.The timeline starts early last Wednesday, when roughly 12 people at Google knew Dean was going. At 8:30 AM he told 139 close colleagues on a video call, and his own summary of it is the most-quoted line of the week: tears, explosions of heart and sad face emojis, lots of chats running on the side of the meeting. If 139 close colleagues sounds implausible, consider that Dean managed about 4,400 people across Google Research and AI, a number that surfaced in Discovery Loop's pitch deck.Half an hour later, two things went out at once: the public announcement of Discovery Loop and the internal farewell email, the one listing MapReduce and BigTable alongside Monterey bike rides and 18 desk moves.By 2:30 PM there was a party. Google had booked a cafe space that holds about 300. Around 1,500 people came.Then Dean, who keeps a group run called "Run or Else…" going, went to a 7 PM yoga session and played a soccer league game at 8:30. He got home at 10:30 PM to those 400 messages.The urgency was technical, not sentimental. Internal chats lived on the corporate account, and the corporate account was expiring. Everything in that inbox would be gone the next day, so he answered all 400 and went to sleep at 2:30 AM. Four hours later he woke to 250 more, plus 500 replies to the farewell email that had CC'd his personal Gmail. At least those won't disappear in eight hours, he noted on the slide.Thursday was a losing race. By 5:20 PM he had cleared nearly every corporate message and they were still arriving. He closed the laptop anyway.At 11:59:59 PM, the slide reads: Unemployed. One second past midnight on Friday, it reads co-founder of Discovery Loop, alongside Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le. The startup is a public benefit corporation backed by Alphabet, Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures, aiming to automate the experimental loop itself and run thousands of AI-designed experiments in parallel across machine learning, chip design and drug discovery. Alphabet is supplying compute for the first year.The exit lands inside a wider AI reshuffle at Google, with Demis Hassabis moving out of the Google DeepMind CEO role into a chairman post and CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu elevated to SVP. Dean followed the KDD slide with a photo of his surrendered badge and sticker-covered Chromebook, captioned "Turned it in…". That post has crossed 2.8 million views.
Article Summary: Jeff Dean, Google's 30th employee and chief scientist, is leaving after 27 years to lead AI startup Discovery Loop. Dean spent his final night as a Google employee doing what most departing executives hand off to an auto-reply. He sat up until 2:30 in the morning answering 400 goodbye messages one by one.

Article Title: Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone isn't dead, but it just lost some glass
Article Text:
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone is still on for 2027, but with less glass than first rumoured.

What actually got cancelled was the more ambitious version

The most talked-about iPhone of 2027 is still happening, just not in the form the rumour mill had settled on. Bloomberg reports that Apple is going ahead with a glass-centric redesign for the iPhone's 20th anniversary next year, with the new look reserved for the Pro models. Glass runs across the front and back and curves into the sides, broken up by a metal band through the middle. The two devices are known internally as V73 and V74.That puts Bloomberg at odds with Jefferies analyst Edison Lee, who told clients earlier this week that supply chain checks showed the all-glass iPhone had been canned over poor yields. Lee called it a major setback for Apple's push into pricier iPhones at a time when memory costs are climbing, and downgraded the stock on the back of it. Bloomberg's sources say the product roadmap hasn't changed at all.Apple's design studio had pushed for a far more aggressive concept that swapped out the metal for even more glass. That one died early. Engineers ran into trouble joining the glass panels together, and the design fell apart once the question turned to manufacturing it in the millions. So the anniversary phone survives as an evolution of the idea rather than the purist version.Timing supports Bloomberg's account. Apple typically locks an iPhone design roughly a year before its September reveal, which means the 2027 phones are already deep in testing.Before any of that, there's next month. Apple is expected to show a foldable iPhone, the biggest change to the product's shape yet, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max with camera upgrades and a new dark red finish. The base iPhone 18, the 18e and a second-generation iPhone Air follow in spring. All of it lands on John Ternus, who becomes CEO on September 1.
Article Summary: Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone is still on for 2027, but with less glass than first rumoured. That one died early. Engineers ran into trouble joining the glass panels together. So the anniversary phone survives as an evolution of the idea rather than the purist version.

Article Title: Subco CEO sends 'urgent message' to Australian Police after two undersea cables damaged, hints at suspicious activity; read message
Article Text:
Image source: Linkedin/Bevan Slattery

What are shunt faults

Subco CEO flags 'suspicious' vessel activity near cable faults

Australian Federal Police confirms investigation

Australia's Federal Police (AFP) is investigating after two undersea communication cables owned by Subco reported faults within minutes of each other. The fault has prompted the company's founder and CEO Bevan Slattery to urge authorities to launch an urgent probe. Slattery said the two cables developed "shunt faults" in close proximity inside a federally protected submarine cable zone off Perth, while what he described as "suspicious/coincidental" activity from a vessel was also recorded near the location at around the same time. The AFP confirmed it had received a report of a crime and is assessing the information.A shunt fault occurs when the insulation around a conductor is damaged, allowing unintended contact with another conductor or the ground, effectively creating a short circuit. Slattery also shared the track of a marine vessel that was allegedly operating near the approximate location of the cable faults when they were detected. However, no evidence has yet linked the vessel to the incident.In a LinkedIn post, Slattery said the Indigo-West cable, which connects Perth to Indonesia and Singapore, and the Indigo-Central cable, which connects Victoria, Tasmania and New South Wales, both reported shunt faults one after another."Earlier tonight: Shunt faults on two systems (Indigo West and Indigo Central) straight after each other and in close proximity to each other. Remarkably this also happened in the Submarine Cable Protection Zone off Perth Australia," he wrote.He added that there was "some suspicious/coincidental activity from a vessel near the location and timing of the shunts occurring."Calling the incident concerning, Slattery said submarine cables are "the digital lifeblood of our nation" and urged the Australian Federal Police to investigate the matter urgently. He also noted that this could become the second such incident inside a federally declared cable protection zone if sabotage is confirmed.Here's what he wrote"Earlier tonight: Shunt faults on two systems (Indigo West and Indigo Central) straight after each other and in close proximity to each other. Remarkably this also happened in the Submarine Cable Protection Zone off Perth Australia.Coincidently some suspicious/coincidental activity from a vessel near the location and timing of the shunts occurring.This is a concerning development. Partially because submarine cables are the digital lifeblood of our nation, but also because this this could very well turn out to be the second such incidence in a Federally declared cable protection zone.This maybe a coincidence, but it’s important for the Australian Federal Police to investigate the issue urgently."The AFP confirmed that it had received a report related to the incident. "The AFP has received a report of crime in relation to this matter," the agency said in a statement, adding that the report is currently being assessed and further comments will be made when appropriate.So far, authorities have not confirmed whether the cables were intentionally damaged.
Article Summary: Two undersea communication cables owned by Subco reported faults within minutes of each other. The fault has prompted the company's founder and CEO Bevan Slattery to urge authorities to launch an urgent probe. Slattery said the two cables developed "shunt faults" in close proximity inside a federally protected submarine cable zone off Perth. The AFP confirmed it had received a report of a crime and is assessing the information.

Article Title: Conservation grants, millions to local schools and more: How Meta managed data center just miles away from Kevin O’Leary’s ‘failed dream project’
Article Text:
Representative Image

Meta's Eagle Mountain data center and early community outreach

"I think we did set some clear expectations in the beginning,"

"Man,"

"these guys really do what they say."

Kevin O'Leary's Project Stratos faces community backlash

"We really scr*wed this up,"

"We have not communicated what we do."

Political fallout in Box Elder County

"We here in the West have a history of overcoming hardships and challenges," she said, adding, "I think [O'Leary] just set himself up for a really big fight [in Box Elder County]."

What comes next for the Utah data center

"I got a lot of work ahead of me,"

"If I've said anything that offends you, yes, I apologize. If I've done anything that you think has been unfair, I apologize. But I also, with that, would say I want you to lend an open ear to what I'm going to show you in the months ahead."

Facebook-parent Meta has been able to do something that Kevin O'Leary has failed to do: win over the local community around its Utah data center. Meta secured approval and support from residents in Eagle Mountain, while O'Leary's Project Stratos in Box Elder County, which is just miles away from the Mark Zuckerberg-led social media giant’s data center has faced sustained backlash since its ‘quiet’ approval in May.Both projects sit on opposite ends of the Great Salt Lake, but the outcomes have diverged sharply. Meta's Eagle Mountain facility, which opened in 2021, is now held up by locals and industry observers as an example of proper community engagement. O'Leary's proposal, by contrast, has become a cautionary tale as developers race to build data centers to meet AI-driven energy demand.Meta broke ground on its Eagle Mountain facility in 2018 and engaged city leaders well before construction began. Mayor Jared Gray told MS Now that the city reached agreements with Meta covering taxation and power usage ahead of time.Gray said.Since opening, Meta has provided conservation grants to 20 organisations across Eagle Mountain, according to Gray. The company has also invested millions of dollars in local schools, funding a hydroponic garden at the high school and providing laptops for every student there.Gray said, describing the town's view of the company,O'Leary's proposal has been shaped by limited outreach and shifting plans. He originally sought to acquire 40,000 acres, an area twice the size of Manhattan, before reducing the footprint by half following community pushback. The project is still expected to draw up to 9 gigawatts of power.Dr Robert Davies, associate professor of physics at Utah State University and a leading critic of the project, compared its power consumption to that of two states of Utah or three New York Cities. He said the resulting heat output could raise temperatures in the valley and speed up evaporation near the Great Salt Lake, which has already lost three-quarters of its volume over several decades.O'Leary acknowledged the communication failures directly.he told MS Now.The approval of Project Stratos carried political consequences almost immediately. Republican voters ousted several local officials who had supported the project in primaries the month after its approval, including the state Senate president.Mare Burningham, who received a Meta grant to study deer migration patterns in Eagle Mountain, described the region's resistance to outside development.O'Leary has since adopted a more conciliatory tone, despite ongoing litigation tied to the project. He told MS Now he still plans to submit permit applications, which would provide the information residents have been requesting.Three months after the project's initial approval, O'Leary's company has not released those plans or disclosed which entity will use the data capacity once built.he said.Meta operates 28 data centers across the US and has faced criticism elsewhere, from concerns over water quality in Georgia to questions about real estate deals in Louisiana. But in Eagle Mountain, the company is seen more as a cooperative presence, a contrast often drawn to the ongoing standoff in Box Elder County.
Article Summary: Meta secured approval and support from residents in Eagle Mountain, Utah. Kevin O'Leary's Project Stratos in Box Elder County has faced backlash since its 'quiet' approval in May. Both projects sit on opposite ends of the Great Salt Lake, but the outcomes have diverged sharply.

Article Title: After Bill Gates' daughter Phoebe Gates' shopping app accused of taking credit for sales it didn't drive, report makes new claim on '24-hour-excuse'
Article Text:
Bill Gates' daughter Phoebe Gates knew about 'cookie stuffing', says report

Internal slack records detail ‘Auto Drop’ features

Code reviews suggest 'automatic refresh of tracking cookies'

Internal communications and software records at Phia, the personal shopping startup co-founded by Bill Gates daughter Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni, indicate that the founders were allegedly aware of software features designed to claim unauthorised sales commissions at least seven months before the company publicly blamed the practice on a sudden “software bug. ” Citing internal Slack messages and source code reviews, Bloomberg reports that the practice, which is known in the affiliate marketing industry as “cookie stuffing”, was active as early as December.The timeline contradicts a public statement issued by the company on July 8, which claimed leadership had only discovered the tracking behavior “within the last 24 hours”.Phia operates as a browser extension designed to help shoppers automatically find discount codes and compare prices at online checkout counters. In exchange, partner retailers pay the platform an affiliate commission when its software helps convert a sale.However, internal chats accessed by the publication reveal that Phia implemented automated features that injected its tracking cookies into a shopper’s checkout session without requiring any user interaction, such as clicking a deal link or applying a coupon code, the Bloomberg report says. By dropping tracking identifiers automatically, Phia claimed credit and commissions for transactions it did not drive, a practice that is strictly prohibited by commercial network contracts and partner agreements.The report further claims that Slack discussions from December show Gates enquiring about whether automated cookie insertion was active across partner sites. In one exchange, Gates asked developers to confirm that “auto pop for cookie drop is live on ALL sites w a coupon to confirm we are monetizing on all gmv [gross merchandise value].”Additional source code reviews showed secondary features, including a “passive trigger” that automatically refreshed tracking cookies every two hours on top retail sites, which essentially increased the likelihood that Phia would overwrite competing referral links and secure the payout.This alleged ‘unauthorised’ attribution strategy generated a substantial portion of the company's daily income. Following the deactivation of these features in early July, Phia’s average daily revenue dropped from approximately $80,000 to between $10,000 and $28,000, the report said.An internal analysis conducted by a company data scientist in July estimated that unauthorised cookie insertion accounted for roughly 51% of the total merchandise value Phia claimed credit for selling in June.A spokesperson for Phia disputed the internal revenue estimates, stating the preliminary analysis relied on an “incorrect methodology.” The company attributed the broader drop in daily income to its decision to pause wider monetisation tools during an internal review.
Article Summary: Bill Gates' daughter Phoebe Gates knew about 'cookie stuffing', says report. Internal slack records detail ‘Auto Drop’ features.Code reviews suggest 'automatic refresh of tracking cookies' Bloomberg reports that the practice, which is known in the affiliate marketing industry as “cookie stuffing”, was active as early as December.

Putting metals in a microwave usually results in sparks. Placing the same piece of metal in an air fryer usually isn't a problem. The difference is not due to luck, but to the fundamental way the two appliances cook food.Safe materials to put in an air fryer include aluminium foil, stainless steel, oven-safe glass and ceramics, food-safe silicone, and small cast-iron pans. These metals pose a problem when placed in the microwave because they reflect microwave radiation, which can cause sparking or arcing. The simple rule is that dry heat combined with airflow, as in air frying, can handle metal while electromagnetic cooking cannot.An air fryer is basically a miniature convection oven. A heating element warms the air in the chamber. A fan is used to blow hot air around the food . The speed of the air is usually between 180 and 200 degree Celsius . That moving heat sears and browns the surface of food via the Maillard reaction, the same chemical process that creates a seared steak or a golden crust on bread.A microwave oven works on a totally different principle. Rather than heating the air around food, it uses electromagnetic waves to excite water molecules within the food, generating heat from the inside.That is why microwaved leftovers tend to be soft or slightly rubbery rather than crisp – there is no dry-surface heat.This very difference is what causes metal to behave so differently in each. In an air fryer, a metal tray or foil liner just conducts and holds heat, as it does in a traditional oven. It is a passive surface. In a microwave, metal reflects electromagnetic waves rather than absorbing them. If that metal is wrinkled, jagged or too close to the cavity wall, the reflected energy can focus and arc, creating sparks that can scorch the appliance or, in rare instances, start a fire.: Foil can line the basket or wrap food directly, as long as it's weighted down by the food so it doesn't lift into the heating element and isn't covering so much surface area that it blocks airflow around the food.They’re okay, provided that they are secured by the food and don’t get caught in the fan. There are also air fryer liners, which are perforated and designed specifically for air fryers, allowing hot air to circulate around the food.: Trays, racks, and small bowls are fine for baking, roasting, or reheating, as long as they fit inside the basket without touching the heating element or blocking airflow from the fan.Oven-safe glass and ceramic dishes are fine for casseroles, small cakes, or baked dishes, as long as they're rated for high heat and sized to fit comfortably. Decorative or handmade ceramics without a heat rating are a different story. They can crack under the dry, direct heat.Food-grade silicone is good for muffins, cakes and individual portions. Small cast-iron skillets can take roasting or baking as long as both are heat-rated and don’t crowd the cooking chamber.Any item marked as microwave-safe does not necessarily mean it can be put in an air fryer, and vice versa. Both types of appliances have been tested at completely different heat levels. For instance, while a plastic container is microwaveable, it might melt under the high dry heat of an air fryer.The placement of the cookware is just as important as the cookware material itself, even if it is heat-safe. A large bowl, solid liner or oversized pan can block the circulation of hot air inside the basket, resulting in uneven cooking, even if nothing melts or burns. Since it is light, unweighted foil or parchment can drift when the fan turns on and sometimes get close enough to the heating element to scorch.Some air fryers add another layer to this. Multi-rack or multi-basket models let you cook at different levels simultaneously, while models with a dehydration setting operate at much lower temperatures, often just 40 to 60°C, for longer periods to slowly draw moisture out of fruit and other foods.Regular plastic containers that aren’t meant for high heat, regular paper towels and glass or ceramic without a heat-safety rating should be avoided altogether when using an air fryer. The reverse is true as well: unrated metal, foil and non-microwave-safe containers should generally be kept out of the microwave unless the appliance’s own manual specifically says otherwise.Yes. You can use it to line the basket or wrap food, as long as it does not block airflow or come into contact with the heating element. The food should hold the foil in place.Metal can reflect microwave energy. Wrinkles, sharp edges or improper placement can cause arcing or sparking that may damage the appliance or create a fire hazard.Yes. Oven-safe stainless steel bowls, trays, and racks work as long as they fit properly and don't restrict airflow or touch the heating element.Yes, when it's suitable for the appliance and held down by food, so it doesn't move toward the heating element or fan.Oven-safe glass and ceramic work if rated for the required temperature and sized to fit comfortably inside the appliance.Not necessarily. Microwave-safe and air-fryer-safe ratings are tested under different heating conditions. A microwave-safe plastic container, for instance, may melt under an air fryer's high dry heat.Check its heat rating, appliance compatibility, and size. The vessel should withstand the cooking temperature without obstructing the circulation of hot air.
Article Summary: Aluminium foil, stainless steel, oven-safe glass and ceramics, food-safe silicone, and small cast-iron pans are safe to use in an air fryer. Air fryer liners, which are perforated and designed specifically for air fryers, allow hot air to circulate around the food.

Article Title: Mayor Zohran Mamdani's 'common sense regulation' that has 'angered' Amazon may impose an extra $664 per year charge on New York households
Article Text:
Zohran Mamdani believes that the bill strengthens worker protections

Amazon pushback against Delivery Protection Act

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has thrown his support behind the Teamsters-based Delivery Protection Act, a bill that would face Amazon and other delivery giants to directly employ thousands of drivers instead of subcontracting last-mile delivery work, according to a report by New York Post. Mamdani called the measure ‘common-sense regulation’ which is designed to protect workers, safeguard communities, and also hold corporations accountable for their business practices. While Mamdani is of the opinion that the bill strengthens worker protections, a study by consultancy AKRF estimates the legislation could add $664 per year to household delivery costs in New York. Critics say the direct-hire mandate would eliminate small businesses that currently operate as Amazon Delivery Service Partners, threatening thousands of jobs and raising prices for consumers.Amazon, which works with more than 40 local partners employing over 5,000 people in the city, warned the legislation could force it to move operations outside New York. “As written, this legislation would directly undermine our commitment — threatening small businesses, putting jobs at risk, and forcing us to consider relocating delivery operations,” said Amazon spokeswoman Kelly A. Nantel.Opposition mountsThe New York Delivers coalition — representing delivery workers and small-business owners — staged a press conference in East Harlem to oppose the bill, arguing it threatens up to 10,000 delivery jobs citywide.Operators like Rudy Cazares, who runs an Amazon partner business employing 130 drivers, said the law would shut down his company. “This direct hire mandate will eliminate every small business out there that delivers packages,” he told The Post.City officials have urged caution, warning of unintended consequences. Council Speaker Julie Menin has said she will wait for the legislative process to unfold before taking a position. Meanwhile, the Teamsters union insists the bill is necessary to curb exploitative subcontracting and strengthen worker rights.Zohran Mamdani sends cease-and-desist notice to Amazon, Walmart and 40 other companiesRecently, Mamdani issued cease and desist notices to 42 online retailers including Amazon, Walmart, Target, Wayfair and Temu parent PDD Holdings, over the sale of allegedly illegal high-speed e-bikes and e-scooters. Mamdani said that the crackdown was important to protect public safety. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Mamdani stated, “Too many lives have been cut short by high-speed, illegal e-bikes and e-scooters. That’s why we are issuing cease-and-desist orders against 42 online retailers that have been selling these dangerous devices to New York City residents — including Target, Temu, Wayfair, Walmart, and Amazon. The safety of New Yorkers is not for sale.” The city said the targeted devices exceed legal limits for speed, weight, or other safety requirements. The action follows a recent crash involving an illegal e-bike that killed a 17-year-old.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has thrown his support behind the Delivery Protection Act. The bill would require Amazon and other delivery giants to directly employ thousands of drivers instead of subcontracting last-mile delivery work. Critics say the direct-hire mandate would eliminate small businesses that currently operate as Amazon Delivery Service Partners.

Article Title: Meta chief technology officer Andrew Bosworth told an employee at townhall: It is very dumb to keep asking for…
Article Text:
Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth

Why Meta's CTO thinks AI productivity gains belong to the product, not the calendar

Meta already tracks what employees type, asking for days off was never going to land

The question was a fair one. If AI is making Meta's engineers measurably faster, could some of that saved time come back to the people doing the work? At a July Q&A, one employee asked whether the productivity gains might fund a revival of Meta Days, the pandemic-era perk that added an extra day off to four long holiday weekends until it was scrapped in 2022.Andrew Bosworth, Meta's chief technology officer, shut it down on the spot. "Stop asking about Meta Days. It's very dumb," he said, per Business Insider, which spoke to three people on the call. Then he explained where he thinks the spare hours should go. Meta has billions of people using its apps daily, he said, and he hopes the extra time goes into building better things for them. He gets an extra hour, he told the room, and that is exactly where he puts it. He wasn't done. Go ask your parents, he suggested, what they make of asking your boss for more days off every time you get his ear.Bosworth apologised afterwards for coming down "too hard," and floated the possibility that the question had been tongue-in-cheek. The position itself stayed exactly where it was. Sam Altman has argued something similar in softer language, saying AI won't shorten the work week because people will just take on more.Bosworth said the quiet part at conversational volume.Meta employees get four weeks off plus public holidays. Meta Days died during the 2022 hiring freeze, in a Q&A where Mark Zuckerberg told staff that some of them probably shouldn't be at the company. Two discretionary "choice days" replaced the perk.What makes the exchange sting is everything around it. Meta cut about 8,000 jobs in May, roughly 10 percent of a 78,000-person workforce, while committing upwards of $125 billion to AI infrastructure this year. The New York Times reported that the company had begun capturing what employees typed, where they clicked and what sat on their screens, to teach its models how people actually use a computer. Asked how to opt out, Bosworth replied that there is no opt-out on a corporate laptop. Over 1,000 employees signed a petition against it.Bosworth stands to collect as much as $921 million from a stock option plan tied to Meta reaching a $9 trillion valuation by 2031. So the productivity question already had an owner before anyone raised a hand. Someone raised a hand anyway, and got told it was dumb.
Article Summary: Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth told employees to stop asking for more days off. He said the extra time would go to building better apps for billions of people. Bosworth apologised for coming down "too hard" on the question. Meta cut about 8,000 jobs in May, while committing upwards of $125 billion to AI infrastructure.
